name: Panvascular-JEPA
description: Abstract Predictive representations for vascular simulation should be tested on unseen network structures and compared with the governing equations before being interpreted as general-purpose world models. We constructed a new, dimensioned but uncalibrated nodal resistance–inertance–compliance benchmark containing all 38 connected, non-isomorphic six-node graphs with five to seven edges. Twenty-four structures supplied training, validation, and new-background testing; 14 structures were wholly withheld. Across 648 parameter backgrounds and two prescribed action programs, 1,296 trajectories contained 96 forecast steps over three cycles. Four graph predictors received equal six-candidate optimization searches, followed by five fixed-seed fits. Selected configurations and analysis code were locked before test trajectories were generated. Comparators included known-equation numerical integrators, an inertia-free reduction, and a five-coefficient model fitted to training trajectories. Unseen-structure mean standardized RMSE was 8.46 × 10 9 for four-factor OPF, 329 for single-factor OPF, and 1.83 × 10 31 for supervised graph prediction, compared with 1.09 × 10 −4 for four-substep known-equation integration and 6.77 × 10 −4 for the fitted mechanism. The primary OPF-4 minus OPF-1 difference was 8.46 × 10 9 , with a paired stratified-graph 95% percentile interval of [2.23 × 10 5 , 2.54 × 10 10 ].
